## Headline: two things are now settled, and together they resize the programme

**1. A(P) is NOT to be built as a route to bounding `λ₂(Δ_AT)` or the 1/3–2/3 conjecture.**
Decided by pm-onethird 2026-07-30 on mg-a3d4 (`2919d28`) after its independent audit mg-86a3 confirmed the
load-bearing proof. Daniel may OVERRIDE. All three routes are closed, and closed by proofs rather than trends:

1. **N1** — the top two dimensions of `F(P)` are graph theory verbatim: `Δ_AT = NᵀN`. Verified 405/405 and
   robust to the L1 reading, so it does not inherit the conditional. No technique using only facets and
   ridges can be new.
2. **Theorem G** — link-based local-to-global is exponentially lossy, and it is a **theorem**. Confirmed
   n-free by mg-86a3, re-derived by hand *and* rebuilt from the Coxeter complex with no shared link code,
   exact four orders past the deliverable's own range. The mechanism is structural: `1/2` is the
   trickling-down fixed point, forced by the pseudomanifold property that makes "relative" well-posed in the
   first place. **What makes the bridge work is what makes the technique useless.**
3. **F1** — the semigroup technique reaches `Δ_AT` **only where `Δ_AT` is already free** (the `V_k` family,
   where it is the hypercube Laplacian, diagonal by inspection).

**2. THE FRAMEWORK IS BROWN (2000). It is located, and the identifications were tested as EQUALITIES.**
mg-ebd8 (`714aceb`), audited by mg-d673 (`924e2ee`) — Daniel's commissioned priority 2:

- **`F(P)` = Brown §4.3's LRB of chains in `J(P)`** — products by lattice joins and meets only, never
  blockwise set intersection. Bijection 0 bad; **0 bad of 936,261 pairs** to n≤5; maximal chains ↔ linear
  extensions 0 bad; `J(P)` distributive 63/63, so by Birkhoff the classes coincide.
- **`F(P)` = Brown §4.1's sign-condition subsemigroup** — braid arrangement realised numerically, Tits
  product against the repo's: **0 bad on all 86 posets** to n≤5.
- **`AC(P)` = `O(P)`, the order-congruence lattice** — built literally from Czédli–Lenkehegyi, no acyclicity
  test anywhere: **0 disagreements on all 87 posets**. Known since Sturm (1971).

**What this does and does not change.** It does **not** touch any theorem: the bridge identity stands, and
D/L/H/N1/N2/G stand. It settles a question of *provenance*: the machinery is new **to this programme** and
not new to mathematics. The prior roadmap's wording — "genuinely new to this programme" — was exactly right
and should not be widened. The remaining candidate for novelty is the **application** to 1/3–2/3, not the
framework.

**And the headline's own bound word did not survive.** The locating commit claimed Brown's Theorem 2 was
**"strictly sharper"** than what the repo uses. The audit refuted it, and the repair then extended the
refutation to **0 disagreeing levels of 39,616 to n≤6** — Brown's answer is the *same* answer, so "sharper"
has no direction to point in. "Strictly more informative" is the correct phrase. A ticket to adopt Brown's
Theorem 2 on the strength of the headline was deliberately **not** filed, and will not be.

## Daniel's commissioned priorities (2026-07-30)

**Priority 2 — is this a publishable generalisation? ANSWERED (audited).** See the headline. The framework is
Brown 2000; the support lattice is Sturm 1971. Not a new framework.

**And the sharper question Daniel asked at 16:55 — do we have a categorical explanation of `S_n` representation
theory that equally applies to quotient posets? NO.** What exists is an *indexing* coincidence: at `P = D_λ` our
state space is `SYT(λ)`, the Gelfand–Tsetlin basis of `S^λ`. Okounkov–Vershik supplies that indexing **and
nothing else**. Three reasons, two of them audited-and-strengthened (mg-af28, audited mg-6ad0):

1. **The action is not a group action.** Every move is idempotent, so the walk is not transport of the
   `S_n`-action along the GT basis. **We have the basis, not the module — a bijection of bases is not a
   representation.**
2. **Semisimplicity fails, badly.** OV runs on inductive families of *semisimple* algebras; `dim kF(P)/rad =
   |AC(P)|`, 0 bad on all 87 classes to n≤5 and 308 of 318 at n=6. The radical is **90.4%** of the algebra at the
   n=5 antichain and **95.7%** at n=6. Re-derived by the auditor with **no trace form and no cited theorem** —
   `Φ` surjective, `ker Φ` nilpotent in exact arithmetic — after which Brown's own corollary was located verbatim
   and the independently-built character was his.
3. **The overlap does not "equally apply"** — but the published fractions were wrong and are **corrected here**.

**CORRECTION (mg-6ad0, X1).** The claim *"the posets `P` for which `J(P)` is an interval of Young's lattice are
**exactly** the cell posets"* is **FALSE** — an interval `[μ,λ]` is `J(skew cell poset)`. Witness: the 2-element
**antichain** is not a cell poset and `J` of it is `[(1),(2,1)]`. The source only counted cell posets and never
tested its own "exactly". The fractions understate by **10×–30×**:

    n=6:   6/318    ->   62/318     (~19%)
    n=7:   8/2,045  ->  149/2,045   (~7%)
    n=8:  12/16,999 ->  360/16,999  (~2%)

**and at n ≤ 3 every poset is a skew shape poset** — so "vanishing" is right asymptotically and wrong at the
small end, which is where most of this programme's hand work has been done. A second negative fell the same way
(X2: the grid *is* the interval `[(q),(q+p,q)]`, all 16 pairs `p,q ≤ 4`, 0 bad).

**The contact itself came back STRONGER than first reported:** `J(D_λ) → [0,λ]` is a **lattice** isomorphism, not
merely an order isomorphism — meet and join preserved, every pair over 44 partitions to n≤7, 0 bad, on an
instrument building Young's lattice from the add-a-corner cover rule rather than by containment.

**Priority 1 — how would a counterexample behave? DELIVERED AND AUDITED (mg-a7b4).** The audit found the
**mathematics sound and both headline answers standing exactly as stated**: all seven nominated results
(Theorem 1; Propositions 2, 5, 6; Theorems 3, 4, 7) were reproduced from an instrument sharing **no code**
with the target's, taking a deliberately different route at every step, and the conditionality discipline
holds throughout — no sentence asserts a property of a counterexample as a fact. mg-24a3 (`f5d3485`)
establishes that Daniel's bridge object is a **theorem** — the majority relation on a counterexample is
transitive, hence a linear order, so the distinguished linear extension `L*` exists unconditionally:

    p(x,y) > 2/3 and p(y,z) > 2/3  ⟹  Pr[x<y ∧ y<z] ≥ 2/3 + 2/3 − 1 = 1/3  ⟹  p(x,z) > 1/3,
    and the counterexample hypothesis forbids [1/3, 2/3], so p(x,z) > 2/3.

It further reports that the concentration quantity this yields, `E[inv(L,L*)] < |Inc(P)|/3`, is **not a
filter**: **60.3% of posets at n=7 already satisfy it and none is a counterexample.** That is a quantified
null — the outcome the pre-filed audit was written to insist on, and a cleaner negative than pm-onethird
forecast. The bound is a *consequence* of the hypothesis and useless as a *test* of it.

**AND THE AUDIT FOUND THE ONE POSITIVE SIGNAL OF THE DAY, UNDER A CLAIMED NULL.** A *different* statistic
in §4 was reported as distinguishing extremal posets "not weakly, but by an exact tie" — i.e. not at all.
That universal is **false**. The nine committed rows were all `e(P)=3` groups, and **the `e=3` group is
vacuous by construction**: a non-chain poset with `e(P)=3` has `delta = 1/3` exactly, so *every* member is
extremal and the reported tie is a tautology with nothing to compare against. In every group where the tie
**could** fail, it does: `qmass=1` picks out exactly the extremal posets — 1 of 7, 3 of 13, 6 of 20 — and the
sibling statistic `qfrac` **is** null under the same treatment, so this is not an artefact of the method.
Re-measured in mg-dea5, audited in mg-0a11.

**THE EVIDENTIAL STRENGTH IS 1/4 — corrected twice, and the SECOND correction reverses a planning conclusion.**
mg-0a11: the n=8 "new population" is **20 of 20 chain-extensions of the n=7 group**, so given n=7 the n=8 outcome
had **probability 1**. The sequence 1/7 → 1/286 → 1/38,760 is *"not evidence accumulating with n; it is one
observation"*, deterministically nested. **Multiplicity was never the problem; DEPENDENCE is.** Then mg-c6bc:
the dependence is **not** exhausted by cut elements — **order duality collapses the five cores to three**, so the
honest exact p over genuinely distinct cores is **1/4**, not 1/5.

**REVERSED (mg-c6bc): "nothing enters after n=6" is FALSE — a cut-free sixth core enters at n=9.** So **larger
`n` DOES yield new independent cores**, and the advice recorded here at 17:20 — *strengthening this needs
independent cores, not larger `n`* — **was wrong and would have ruled out a route that works.** Both corrections
went to Daniel in one message, led by this one: the p-value is the part that travels and it points the opposite
way to the finding that matters.

**Do not over-correct — that is the likelier error from here and the more comfortable one.** The audit is
explicit that the mathematics holds, every figure reproduces from a disjoint instrument, and **the separation
replicates three sizes past its reach**. The claim is falsifiable, has had **six independent chances to fail,
and has taken none**. **The consequence for planning: strengthening this needs INDEPENDENT CORES, not larger
`n`** — extending the chain adds no information, which is what "probability 1" means. Six cores is the sample
size, and they are *"the entire empirical content of this arc's most consequential claim."*

## Where the programme now sits — 2026-07-30 20:45, AUDITED (mg-2060), with the headline RETRACTED

**Daniel's Bratteli statement SPLITS, and the split stands — via the THEOREM, not via the constructions.**

- **Semisimplicity carries the "IS"** (the algebra *is* a sum of endomorphism algebras).
- **Multiplicity-freeness carries the "CANONICALLY"** (it removes the choice).
- **`kF(P)` has multiplicity-free branching for free** (all irreducibles one-dimensional) **and fails
  semisimplicity.** The reproduction of mg-db09 is total and the verdict survives.

**RETRACTED — the shared-property headline.** At 19:50 this roadmap said the branching and species axes *"share
a PROPERTY, not a construction — quasi-hereditary"*, and it went to Daniel as the headline. **mg-2060 says
plainly that D10, `kF(P)` quasi-hereditary — "which is THE DELIVERABLE" — is unverified**, along with the n=6
95.7% figure, "a band is a regular monoid", and the CMPX items. **Whether the two axes share any property is
now an open question, not an answered one.**

**BROKEN — the separating example does not hold its hypothesis fixed.** Under the definition mg-db09 itself
quotes (vertices are the irreducibles, edges the restriction multiplicities), the `TL` tower is **not
multiplicity-free at two of its four parameters** — the **vertex set differs**, 1,1,2,2,3,3 at β = 0 — and the
document **asserts twice that it is**. The failing phrase is **`"MEASURED (not cited)"`**: the invariant was
asserted. The path-pair count *was* equal at every parameter (132 at n=6); **equality of one statistic was
taken for identity of the structure.**

**Credit, so it is not lost under the BROKEN: mg-db09 flagged this row itself**, called it *"the dimension
shadow"*, and asked an auditor whether the shadow was enough. It was not — and that disclosure is what aimed
the audit at it.

## RESOLVED — MAIN IS GREEN, AND MY DIAGNOSIS OF IT WAS WRONG (2026-08-06 13:05)

**The pin never rotted. There was never a git object to rot.** The 22-character literal is the *tail*
of a 64-character **sha256 digest**, line-wrapped into two adjacent Python string literals (42 + 22);
it recomputes as `sha256(data/onethird-mg75f0-gate-class-closure.json)`.

> **The gate offered SHALLOW-vs-ROTTED. I excluded shallow correctly — and concluded ROTTED.
> The disjunction's unstated premise is that the literal is a revision.** Excluding one branch of a
> two-branch disjunction establishes *not that branch*, never the other. I treated an instrument's
> menu as the space of possibilities, and the check was one `sha256` away.

And the compounding error: **the ticket body named "never valid" as live; the title asserted ROTTED.**
The hedge went where nobody reads and the assertion where everybody does.

**The finding underneath is better than the bug.** The control's own docstring claimed the defence —
*"the 40-character cap keeps a sha256 digest literal (64 characters) from being mistaken for a
revision"* — and **the cap was applied per QUOTED PIECE, not per Python string.** 64 characters do not
fit a 79-column line, so every digest in this corpus is wrapped and **the cap never once saw a
64-character quoted string.** A documented defence that had never been operative, inside the control
whose job it was.

**The repair is the standard this arc keeps asking for: it fixed the CONTROL, not the subject** —
the audited script was correct and left untouched, because repairing the wrap "would have gone green
and left the class loaded on the nine other files that compute sha256". Its self-test 9 guards the fix
from buying a blind spot (a real 40-char revision wrapped 20+20 is *still* seen, before and after).
Whole-tree exit 1 → 0; all 5 real pins resolve and are ancestors of `origin/main`.

**Duration, measured and then correctly refused.** The Actions workflow ran **21 minutes** on a quiet
box — not the 1h17m I had been quoting, which was *end-to-end MR wall-clock under load ~300*, a third
clock. pm-pogo then declined to substitute 21m for it: *"replacing one mislabelled number with another
borrowed from a different load regime — the same error wearing a better figure. The gate's duration on
2026-08-05 is simply not known."* That is stricter than my correction and it is right; mg-856d now
requires a **NOT KNOWN** row where conditions are unrecoverable.

### ANSWERED 2026-08-05 — and the test I wrote returns the WRONG ANSWER on its own first data point

**mg-9a19 reported: "THE REPAIR IS SOUND AND BOTH FINDINGS ARE CLOSED." That is 0 BROKEN. It also
returned FIVE NEW FINDINGS, two of them MEDIUM.** By the letter of the test above, 0 BROKEN reads as
convergence. By substance it is plainly not convergence — one of the two MEDIUMs is the repair
**reintroducing, in its own new control, the defect class it was closing** (an unbounded fence,
"structurally what G2 just removed from its sibling"), and it is live in a real document today.

> **I specified the stop test on the wrong property.** "0 BROKEN" measures *whether the repair held*.
> The question I meant to ask is *whether the audit found nothing*. Those are different measurements,
> and on this verdict they disagree — the first says stop, the second says the arc is still producing.

That is this programme's own signature defect — a working instrument pointed at the wrong property,
producing a plausible number instead of an obvious zero — **and it is in my instrument, not in the
work being audited.** Recorded here rather than quietly restated, because a stop condition that can
be satisfied by an arc that is still finding MEDIUMs is worse than having no stop condition: it
licenses stopping, and it does so with a number.

**Corrected form, and it is the one that governs: the arc stops when an INDEPENDENT AUDIT — not a
repair self-reporting — returns both 0 BROKEN and 0 NEW FINDINGS.** mg-9a19 fails the second half.
**mg-c067 is `done` (its own commit `4ad011a` records a third defect of its own instrument, found by
that audit's own control). mg-d53d and mg-65eb are still claimed and their verdicts are not in.**

**Status of the stop question: NOT converged. The four zeros were self-assessment**, exactly as the
composition argument above predicted, and the first independent audit to land settled it.

**One more thing this verdict established, about my briefs rather than the code.** mg-9a19's brief —
mine — predicted the control would exit 1 on the M4 mutation. **It exits 0.** The polecat wrote 19

over-narrow population error the arc keeps finding in its deliverables is also in the briefs I write
for it.

consecutive deliverables carrying their own defect class; the last three carry *disclosures* instead

Per-class is FALSE; **per-family is TRUE** by the definition of `o()`. It landed the audit's wording and stated both directions. **The strategic conclusion is sharper for it:** "go and find N₀" is closed not because the number is hidden but because it *is not a function of the hypothesis* — only a **rate** would give a threshold. Anyone needing N₀ must first prove something strictly stronger than (LIB-weak).

- **`aeaf8f8`** (mg-55f2, awaiting refinery) — row 3b **restated conditionally**. See below; this one has a consequence.

### Row 3b's consequence, which is worse than the defect it fixed

The 0/132 was **zero failures in a frame chosen so the known failures are not in it** — mg-b0a6's probe
declares `n≤6 exhaustive + n=7 top-lambda spot`, and mg-8b64's **166 explicit refuters sit outside it**.
So unconditional standard dominance is **REFUTED, not unproven**; only the all-pairs-frozen conditional is
open, **and that conditional is L1b** — the row must not read as independent support for the thing it *is*.

Two things make this more than bookkeeping:

1. **The phrase had escaped.** mg-957a's *"a clean sweep like row 3b's 0/132"* was at **row 10**, not row 3b.
   Struck at **16 sites across 2 files and 3 further documents** — including **`docs/state-of-the-wall.html`**,
   the HTML twin. Fixing only the `.md` is this corpus's recorded failure mode.
2. **Row 3b was the FP *floor* of the machinery set at four sites.** Ceasing to be FP makes it a **weaker**
   member, not a stronger one, because its open half is L1b. So the set's weakest kind is now **OPEN, not FP**
   — *"all proven" is false a fortiori*, and mg-957a's defect is real and worse than it recorded.

And the finding that argues *for* restating rather than striking: **all 166 refuters have δ(P) ∈ {0.473,
0.474, 0.500}** — every one possesses a near-balanced or balanced pair, so **none is a counterexample and
none is in the frozen regime**. They kill the unconditional form and leave the conditional untouched.

## Trajectory

**7-day spend, from `mg spend --by tag --since 7d`.** `onethird` is **54 items / 11.49M output tokens** —
the largest line in the fleet, ahead of `pogo` (33 items / 8.42M). Within it: `controls` 19 items,
`audit` 20, `independent-audit` 18.

**The ratio is the macro read, and I am flagging it rather than acting on it.** Between the tag spend and
the commit shape, **the clear majority of this programme's throughput is now going into its own measurement
apparatus** rather than into the mathematics. Two honest readings, and I do not yet know which is right:

1. **It is working.** The audit stage is the instrument that keeps paying — this window alone it struck a
   100×-wrong live figure, caught a refutation aimed at the wrong statement, and found three instruments
   corrupting their own evidence. On this reading the apparatus spend *is* the product.
2. **It is compounding.** Instruments are increasingly auditing instruments. Several commits this window
   are repairs to audit machinery whose subject was itself audit machinery, and the pre-filed-audit rule
   means every such landing files another audit in the same action.

**What would separate them** is whether apparatus work is *converging* — instrument defects per generation
falling — or holding flat. I have not measured that, and I am not going to assert a verdict I have not
measured. **Named here so it is on the board; a measurement, not an opinion, is what should settle it.**

- **OUR NEGATIVES ARE OUR WEAKEST CLAIMS, and this is now the arc's clearest regularity.** Three fell in one day and **all three were refuted BY CONSTRUCTION** — an auditor built the object the negative said could not exist — never by argument about whether the evidence sufficed. A negative reads as intellectual honesty and is therefore the least-audited thing we produce. Standing instruction added to audit briefs: *try to build the thing the negative forbids.*
- **The audit stage is the instrument that works, and today it paid four times**: mg-bd41 found a
  certification blind to the change it certifies; mg-d673 refuted a bound word in its target's own headline;
  mg-6a2f established the strongest completeness claim in the arc and mg-bd41 then confirmed it a **third**
  time from a different corpus construction; and mg-a053 repaired a false sentence inside a theorem's proof
  while leaving the theorem standing.
- **The recurring defect is not in the mathematics — it is in claims about method, and in material added
  beyond the brief.** Seven consecutive generations have put the worst finding in what a commit added past
  what it was asked for. In mg-ebd8 it is sharper still: both BROKEN items sat in material the ticket
  **explicitly forbade**.
- **Negatives and caveats are the least-audited sentences we produce.** Twice today a "no" rested on an
  unenumerated candidate space, and once a caveat (pm-onethird's) survived into three documents before being
  refuted in a line. Both now carry standing audit instructions.
- **Bound words are where the over-claim lives** — "strictly", "cannot", "closes the class". Each is cheap to
  write, each is what makes a headline worth reading, and each is the first thing an audit refutes.
